# Generative and Latent Space Optimization

Also called: GenN2N, 3D VAE-GAN

## Overview
This family optimizes 3D representations by learning a latent distribution of edits or textures conditioned on 2D inputs or text prompts, rather than optimizing raw voxel/grid parameters directly. It differs from standard differentiable volume rendering [43-differentiable-volume-rendering.md] by treating the 3D scene as a sample from a generative model (e.g., a VAE-GAN) or by optimizing explicit geometric primitives (meshes) using score distillation, thereby enabling high-level semantic control and multi-view consistency through latent space constraints.

## Shared principles
The core mechanism involves mapping 2D observations or text prompts into a latent space, which then conditions a 3D generative model or an optimization loop. Gradients are propagated from 2D losses (reconstruction, adversarial, or SDS) through a differentiable renderer back to the latent codes or explicit parameters. The key distinction from direct parameter optimization is the introduction of a latent distribution constraint (e.g., KL divergence to a Gaussian) or a distillation loss that aligns rendered views with a pre-trained 2D prior.

## Subtopics

### [Generative NeRF-to-NeRF Translation](17067-generative-nerf-to-nerf-translation.md)
A unified framework that lifts 2D image edits to 3D by modeling the distribution of edited Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) via a conditional generative model. Unlike task-specific editing methods, it employs a plug-and-play 2D image-to-image translator to generate edited views, then learns a latent distribution of 3D edits to ensure multi-view consistency. It achieves all NeRF editing tasks by performing editing in the 2D domain and lifting 2D edits into the 3D NeRF space. Choose this when you need a general-purpose, plug-and-play solution for diverse NeRF editing tasks (text, style, super-resolution) without retraining a separate model for each task.

### [Mesh Texture Optimization via SDS](18733-mesh-texture-optimization-via-sds.md)
This method optimizes the vertex texture map of a fixed 3D mesh geometry to match a text prompt using Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) gradients, without modifying the mesh vertices or faces. It differs from NeRF optimization by optimizing explicit vertex colors rather than implicit volumetric fields, and from image optimization by operating on a 3D geometric primitive with consistent lighting. Choose this when you have a fixed mesh geometry and want to apply text-driven texture synthesis using diffusion priors.

### 3D VAE-GAN
A generative model that encodes 2D edited images and decodes 3D NeRFs, using a differentiable volume renderer to connect 3D content creation with 2D GAN losses [S1]. The process involves encoding edited images into latent edit codes, decoding these codes into a NeRF representation, and rendering multi-view images from the NeRF using a differentiable volume renderer [S1]. A 2D adversarial loss is applied to the renderings to supervise 3D generation, ensuring that inconsistent multi-view renderings help each other regarding 3D generation [S1]. This approach was proposed to model the distribution of underlying 3D edits through a generative model that can cover all possible edited NeRFs, incorporating a differentiable volume renderer to connect 3D content creation with 2D GAN losses [S1].

## Background
The concept of using generative models for 3D editing emerged as NeRFs gained popularity for their high-quality novel view synthesis but lacked easy editing capabilities. The GenN2N paper [S1] introduced the idea of modeling the distribution of 3D edited NeRFs from 2D edited images using a 3D VAE-GAN. This allows users to sample from the conditional generative model to obtain various 3D editing results aligned with editing goals, such as text-driven editing, colorization, and inpainting. The integration of differentiable rendering with GAN losses ensures that the generated 3D content remains consistent across views despite the stochastic nature of 2D generation.
